fix(mysql): parse the AS clause of WEIGHT_STRING [CLAUDE] (#8544)

WEIGHT_STRING(str AS CHAR(N)) and WEIGHT_STRING(str AS BINARY(N)) failed
with "Expecting )". Parse them into a new WeightString expression that
keeps the type in `to`. Calls with any other number of arguments, such as
the undocumented WEIGHT_STRING(str, n, n, n) form that MySQL also accepts,
stay Anonymous with the name as written.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+    def test_weight_string(self):
+        for sql in (
+            "SELECT WEIGHT_STRING('ab')",
+            "SELECT WEIGHT_STRING('1' AS CHAR(1))",
+            "SELECT WEIGHT_STRING('ab' AS BINARY(4))",
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(sql):
+                self.validate_identity(sql).selects[0].assert_is(exp.WeightString)
+
+        self.validate_identity("SELECT WEIGHT_STRING('ab', 0, 3, 0)").selects[0].assert_is(
+            exp.Anonymous
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            self.parse_one("SELECT weight_string('ab', 0, 3, 0)").selects[0].name, "weight_string"
+        )
